subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 be fixed as unintended DeepSeek-session promotion on Codex hot reload, treated as expected explicit /model openai/* pin behavior with better recovery guidance, or folded into the broader #87957 session-state resolver?
rationale: Source proves that DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the report mixes plugin hot reload, persisted session state, and a later explicit /model openai clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract.

options.title: Confirm then repair session state
options.body: Reproduce the hot-reload path and fix the selected/runtime state owner so Codex enablement cannot promote an unpinned DeepSeek session.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI pin as expected
options.body: If the explicit /model openai/* pin is the whole trigger, keep routing unchanged and improve status or doctor guidance around /model default.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Make #87957 canonical only after copying this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload acceptance case into that broader session-state refactor.

recommendation.title: Confirm then repair session state
recommendation.body: Reproduce the hot-reload path and fix the selected/runtime state owner so Codex enablement cannot promote an unpinned DeepSeek session.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-file history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex harness behavior, and session/model routing surfaces.
